\[
D = \sqrt{d_c^2 + \left(\frac{d_s}{S}\right)^2 m^2},
\qquad
S = \sqrt{N / K}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(d_c, d_s\): The distances in CIELAB color and in position
- \(S\): The grid step of the starting centers
- \(m\): The compactness

N is the number of pixels and K the number of superpixels, so the centers start on a grid with the step S. Each pixel is compared with the centers within 2 S of it. The distance D joins the color distance d_c in CIELAB and the distance in position d_s, scaled by S and the compactness m. Each pixel joins its nearest center, the centers move to the mean color and position of their pixels, and this repeats. Finally, parts of superpixels that are cut off join a neighbor, so every superpixel is connected. Searching only near each center makes it linear in the number of pixels.
